Congenital duplication and triphalangism of index-like digits; localized skeletal malformation.
Familial benign bone tumors arising in the cranial vault; skull location does not imply brain involvement.
Grade 3 oligodendroglioma is a primary central nervous system tumor.
Corticospinal tract degeneration defines this pure spastic paraplegia. Weakness is neurogenic; urinary urgency is occasional and does not establish urinary tract damage.
Diabetic metabolic microangiopathy directly damages retinal capillaries and retina; capillaries fall within the cardiovascular axis.

Cohen alias ([Orpha](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/2829)); ID, retinal dystrophy, neutropenia; joint laxity >30% ([cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1181995/)); obesity capped.
Inherited degeneration of motor neurons defines the group; weakness and denervation do not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Congenital structural abnormalities of kidneys and urinary tract; renal hypoplasia in 6/12.
Severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; fixed limb contracture in 1/1 assessed supports skeletal involvement. AV block lacks evidence of persistent intrinsic cardiac disease.
Congenital heart defects include VSD in 3/9 and other lesions; strabismus in 3/9 (~33%) supports ocular involvement. Individual skeletal defects occur in 1/9.
Viral infection of nasal and nasopharyngeal mucosa; upper airways belong to the pulmonary axis.
Progressive cerebellar and pyramidal degeneration; nystagmus and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction. Skeletal deformities are occasional.
Growth hormone resistance with immune dysregulation defines disease; eczematoid dermatitis directly affects skin in 2/3 assessed (~67%).
Verrucous squamous carcinoma originates in plantar skin; foot location alone does not imply bone or muscle involvement.
Monoclonal B-cell lymphoma, usually localized to peripheral lymph nodes; marrow, spleen and liver involvement are occasional.
Brain calcification with neurodegeneration defines disease; localized calcification does not establish systemic calcium or endocrine disease.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss and characteristic myopathy, with abnormal muscle biopsy in 5/5; hepatic steatosis in 1/3 supports hepatic involvement near the threshold.
Ammonia excess; encephalopathy/coma common in symptomatic cases ([review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9726343/)). Frequency across asymptomatic forms is uncertain.
Bilateral structural deformity of the distal radius and wrist.
Bone fragility, developmental disability and sensorineural hearing loss define syndrome; high myopia in 3/4. Cap omits enamel defects (5/5) and microcytic anemia (4/4).
Endometrial tissue confined to uterine myometrium; reproductive organs have no axis. Menorrhagia alone does not establish hematologic disease.
Tympanic membrane inflammation, usually viral or bacterial ([reference](https://gesund.bund.de/en/trommelfellentzuendung)); no other organ involvement established.
Localized HPV infection producing an epithelial wart in plantar skin.
Abnormally increased bone density defines this bone remodeling disorder; no additional organ damage is established across the umbrella.
